extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems from high school math competitions, each with a full step-by-step solution and final boxed answer, tagged by subject and difficulty.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks; Collin Burns; Saurav Kadavath; Akul Arora; Steven Basart; Eric Tang; Dawn Song; Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.citeAs: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, and Jacob Steinhardt. Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset. NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Problems were collected from mathematics competitions including AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more, many from the AoPS community site. Problems were categorized by subject and AoPS difficulty level, and consistently formatted in LaTeX and Asymptote.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Competition mathematics problems and solutions from AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and other contests, many collected from the AoPS community site.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Final boxed answers were normalized with consistent formatting rules so equivalent answers could be matched exactly; equivalent fraction, parenthesis, spacing, unit, numeric, and factor order variants were treated as equivalent.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems and solutions were consistently formatted in LaTeX and Asymptote, and final answers were wrapped in \boxed{} with normalization rules to enable automatic exact-match evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem includes subject and difficulty labels, with difficulty encoded from 1 to 5 following AoPS. Problems also include step-by-step solutions and final boxed answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Equivalent answer forms were analyzed and normalized so that exact-match scoring would treat practically equivalent outputs as the same answer.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note potential misuse for cheating on homework or exams and state that they do not intend the dataset to train models that help students cheat; they intend it to help forecast reasoning capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset reflects mathematics competitions in the United States and assesses the abilities of top young mathematical talent in the United States.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging even for strong models; scaling current Transformers appears insufficient for strong performance, and solving it may require new algorithmic advances. The authors also note non-recommended use for helping students cheat on mathematics exams.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and measuring mathematical problem-solving ability of machine learning models; training/fine-tuning models using problems, final answers, and step-by-step solutions; pretraining with the auxiliary AMPS corpus.

name.evidence: To measure the problem-solving ability of machine learning models, we introduce the MATH dataset, which consists of 12,500 problems from high school math competitions.

description.evidence: Many intellectual endeavors require mathematical problem solving, but this skill remains beyond the capabilities of computers. To measure this ability in machine learning models, we introduce MATH, a new dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems. Each problem in MATH has a full step-by-step solution... In addition, MATH problems are tagged by difficulty from 1 to 5, and span seven subjects...
